thread:
mike.h: Heads up — git leak scanner just flagged a git-lfs object in a submodule (third_party/etl) that looks like an environment service token.

devsec-bot: automated scan result: `git-lfs-object` match, blob sha: 5f3c9a8, flagged by rule `lfs-service-token-regex`. Confidence 0.92.

lina: can you paste the pointer / path and which commit introduced it?

mike.h: path: third_party/etl/vendor/credentials.bin (LFS pointer). commit: f1a2b3c -> the submodule commit points at 9c8d7e. scanner output attached.

mike.h: snippet:```
version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1
Oid sha256:5f3c9a8...
Size 2048
```

kevin: is this an internal service account token or external vendor token?

mike.h: looks like an internal ephemeral service token (starts "rwd-svc-"), probably used by legacy ETL job deployed by infra years ago.

ops_jordan: immediate actions: 1) revoke token now, 2) rotate any CI secrets referencing it, 3) create incident ticket. I'll revoke and post audit ID.

ops_jordan: (revoked) done — token revoked in IAM at 1972468123. audit_id=IAM-AUDIT-1972468123. Notifying oncall.

simone: thanks. can we confirm whether CI used that token in any pipelines? grep across repo + CI env vars?

mike.h: already ran `rg "rwd-svc-" -S` across org repos and CI configs — two hits: infra/ci/etl-deploy.yml and a legacy personal pipeline in ops/jordan's fork. I've opened SEC-2026 to track.

lina: for containment, since this is an LFS blob in a submodule, normal git filter-branch won't touch it. We need to: 1) purge LFS object from the LFS store, 2) rotate/replace submodule commit / reupload clean pointer, 3) consider history rewrite on the submodule repo only.

kevin: suggested commands to inspect LFS objects:```bash
git lfs ls-files --all
git lfs fetch --all
git lfs pointer --file=third_party/etl/vendor/credentials.bin
```

mike.h: to purge the object from the public LFS store we asked vendor-hosting to delete blob sha 5f3c9a8 and to clear cache. I've filed a deletion request with host (ticket HOST-4521).

simone: ops_jordan, after revoke please rotate any KMS-wrapped secrets and check KMS audit logs for any decrypt calls tied to that key. If the token was generated from an automation that used KMS unwrap, rotate key material and rotate automation to short lived tokens.

ops_jordan: KMS audit shows no decrypt activity from that key in the last 90 days for that token ID — looks like token was committed but not used in recent runs. still rotating KMS key used by ETL as precaution.

lina: post-mortem/next steps: 1) document incident in SEC-2026, 2) add pre-receive LFS pointer denylist rule for our org (prevent push of pointers that match token regex), 3) add LFS scanning to pre-merge checks in CI, 4) schedule history rewrite for submodule repo owners (BFG or git filter-repo) and coordinate with downstream integrators.

kevin: add RBAC mitigation: limit service token scopes to least privilege, enforce expiration, and move to short-lived tokens via Vault/GCP IAM/workflows; create a migration plan.

mike.h: quick temp mitigation: added a pre-receive hook on main repo to block pushes that include `third_party/etl` submodule changes until submodule is cleaned. Hook id: pre-recv-1972468320.

devsec-bot: created incident SEC-2026 and linked to jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026. Assigned: lina. Priority: P2.

lina: assigning remediation owners: submodule cleanup -> ops_jordan + vendor team; scanning + pre-merge hook -> devex; RBAC/KMS plan -> kevin + simone; postmortem writeup -> mike.h.

mike.h: rough timeline: revoke done, host deletion request filed, pre-receive block in place, CI rotations started. scheduling submodule history rewrite with vendor for next week.

simone: reminder: update audit logging retention to include LFS delete events and add alert when new LFS blobs match sensitive patterns.

kevin: will follow up with a short RFC for moving tokens out of repo and into KMS/Vault with automated short-lived issuance.

ops_jordan: I'll post an update in #incidents once host confirms blob deletion.

mike.h: thanks everyone. will draft post-incident checklist and share in SEC-2026. :thumbsup:
